### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | *(see summary — defaults to publisher-level policy unless a journal-specific override was found)* |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | conditional |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 |
| **Summary** | OUP/Mind requires mandatory disclosure of any Gen AI use (content generation, images, code, data processing, translation) both in the cover letter to editors and in the Methods/Acknowledgements section; authors must complete an AI Use Declaration Form. AI tools (e.g. ChatGPT) cannot be listed as authors. This is OUP's general policy, surfaced on Mind's own General Instructions page (not a Mind-specific bespoke policy). |
| **Source URL** | https://academic.oup.com/mind/pages/General_Instructions |

### Preprint Policy

> AI-research note (not broken down per-stage): Yes — OUP's Self-Archiving Policy B applies: authors may post their Author's Original Version (AOV, i.e. pre-refereeing preprint) anywhere, at any time, with no embargo. This is OUP's general journal self-archiving policy, not a Mind-specific preprint statement.
> Source: https://academic.oup.com/pages/self_archiving_policy_b

### Orientation

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Empirical vs. Theoretical** | *(pending — no evidentiary basis collected; would require reading a sample of recent articles)* |
| **Quantitative vs. Qualitative** | *(pending)* |
| **Cross-disciplinary openness** | *(pending)* |

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** Mind is a deliberately generalist philosophy journal: since a 2015 editorial shift it accepts work from every area, style, and school of philosophy (previously it was analytic-only). Quality is stated as the sole criterion. The current editorial team (handover summer 2025) explicitly wants to broaden further into continental philosophy and history of philosophy while preserving the analytic tradition.

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** Traditional analytic argumentation (epistemology, metaphysics, philosophy of language, philosophy of logic, philosophy of mind), Continental philosophy (newly and explicitly welcomed since 2015, reaffirmed by 2025 incoming editors), History of philosophy, No area/style/school formally excluded per journal's own statement

### AI-Research Notes (sources, blanks, and cross-language checks)

**Sources cited across this entry:**
- https://academic.oup.com/mind/pages/General_Instructions
- https://academic.oup.com/mind/pages/why-submit
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mind_(journal)
- https://mindassociation.org/2024/05/27/mind-journal-seeks-to-appoint-new-editors/
- https://scirev.org/journal/mind/

**Fields deliberately left blank, and why:**
- **experiential.reviewer_culture**: No first-hand forum discussion found. Searches on Reddit r/AskAcademia and r/askphilosophy, muchong.com (小木虫), zhihu, and fabiaoji-style Chinese sites returned no substantive first-hand posts about Mind's reviewer tone/culture — only generic journal-metrics aggregator pages and the journal's own boilerplate. Left null rather than inventing a narrative.
- **experiential.desk_reject_pct**: No first-hand numeric source. SciRev shows 'n/a' (sample too small: 5 reviews). Journal's own page says 'most' submissions desk-rejected but gives no percent. A third-party aggregator (editage/journalsinsights-style) claims 13.2% acceptance but is not first-hand and its methodology is unverifiable, so it was excluded rather than presented as fact.
- **ai_policy.gate/leniency source specificity**: The AI policy found is OUP's house-wide policy reproduced on Mind's General Instructions page; no Mind-specific carve-out or stricter/looser rule was found, so this is publisher-level, not journal-bespoke.
- **positioning special-issue CFP**: No current (2024-2026) special issue or CFP was found for Mind; it runs occasional thematic 'Virtual Issues' (e.g. Aesthetics, Evidence) which are retrospective collections of already-published papers, not open calls for new submissions, so no CFP framing requirement could be extracted.
- **cross_language sources with zero yield**: 小木虫 (muchong.com) direct search returned no Mind-specific thread (only tangential hits for other journals like Minds and Machines); 知乎 (zhihu) search returned no Mind-specific discussion; fabiaoji was not reachable via general web search and returned no hits. These are recorded as 0-result checks, not skipped.

**Cross-language checks performed (mandatory per methodology):**
- 小木虫 muchong.com: searched 'Mind 期刊 哲学 投稿' — 0 Mind-specific results (only unrelated journal threads and aggregator SEO pages surfaced)
- 知乎 zhihu: searched 'Mind 哲学期刊 投稿 审稿' — 0 first-hand zhihu results surfaced (search returned only English OUP/Wikipedia pages)
- gwyoo.com (Chinese SCI journal info aggregator): page titled 'Mind-审稿速度' found but contained no concrete review-speed figure ('投稿过审时间平均-' left blank on the page itself), only a vague qualitative note that review times are 'generally long' for this 'top-tier' journal
- fabiaoji: no results found via web search, likely not indexed/reachable for this query
- Reddit r/AskAcademia and r/askphilosophy: searched multiple queries — 0 relevant threads specifically about Mind (philosophy journal) surfaced
- SciRev (English, but a query-time experiential data source): found — 5 reviews, 6.3-month first round, 14.4-month total handling, 3.4/5 review-report quality, 2.6/5 overall handling score
